sources.title: Scientists predicted Friday 13 November 2026 will be ‘Doomsday.’ Should you be worried?

discussion.body: The unsettling part is not that a forecast failed. It is how long a well-fitted curve can look right. This one survived more than three decades of citations before reality drifted off it.

Calling it accurate until 1993 flatters it. A forecast that names a specific doomsday can be wide of the mark for decades before the miss becomes visible; 1993 is when the error got large enough to notice, not when it started.

items.title: A 1960 Doomsday Forecast Names This November — and Held Up Until 1993
items.body: In 1960, the journal Science published an article predicting that on 13 November 2026 the human population would approach infinity. That date falls this November, which makes the paper's afterlife more interesting than its prediction. The article was regularly cited, and its forecasts appeared remarkably accurate — until around 1993, halfway to the predicted date, when global population growth began falling behind them. Which is the usable lesson: a projection can track decades of data and still misdescribe what comes next, because the parameters that fit the past are not promises about the future. Growth stopped following the curve, and the doomsday date became an artifact of a model rather than a deadline.

sources.title: Disgust, Desire, and Durian

discussion.body: For anyone who has not met one, the American botanist Francis Ramaley's 1905 attempt to describe the smell is a good starting point: a rare combination of vile odors, he wrote, moving from rotten eggs to sewer gas to garlic before giving up on classifying it at all.
The market is the real rebuttal to the smell. Revulsion is not rejection — people simply disagree about what the fruit is worth enduring.

items.title: Durian Emptied a Library in 2019. It Also Fuels a Multibillion-Dollar Trade.
items.body: In 2019, 550 students evacuated the University of Canberra's library because of durian. Its sulfuric odor had been mistaken for a gas leak — and according to JSTOR Daily, that kind of false alarm is common enough to have grounded planes and baffled fire departments. Then there is the other half of the fruit's reputation: despite the smell, durian's sweet flesh has built a multibillion-dollar consumer market that the article says fuels economic growth in Vietnam, Malaysia, Cambodia and Thailand. Disgust and appetite rarely share an object this openly. The smell that reads as danger to a fire alarm and the fruit that reads as luxury to a buyer are the same thing.

sources.title: Canada promised a new citizenship guide that better addresses reconciliation a decade ago. It still hasn’t arrived

items.title: Canada's Citizenship Study Guide Is Nearly 17 Years Old, and Its Replacement Has Been Promised for a Decade
items.body: The citizenship study guide that would-be Canadians work from largely leaves out settler colonialism, the Indian Act and the ongoing legacy of residential schools, and it is nearly 17 years old. Ottawa has been promising to replace it for the last decade. Meanwhile, research published in The Conversation Canada describes interviews with eight citizenship educators working in two large non-profit community organizations in Vancouver, B.C. — the people handling a gap that official material has not closed. That gap matters beyond exam preparation. For many newcomers, the guide is one of the first official versions of Canada they encounter, so what it omits is itself a message about what the country chooses to teach about itself.

sources.title: Query claims in natural language with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases

items.title: What Managed Retrieval Does With a Scattered Claim File
items.body: Insurance claim answers do not sit in a field. They are spread across adjuster diary entries, repair estimates, police reports, payment ledgers and scanned attachments. Retrieval-augmented generation is aimed at exactly that shape of problem: instead of answering from model memory, you retrieve the relevant documents and make the model answer from them. On AWS, Amazon Bedrock handles the parsing, chunking, embeddings and vector storage, which lets a builder put a conversational interface on top that returns cited answers drawn from claim files. One caveat belongs in view: the vendor's walkthrough uses synthetic claim records and does not describe a production customer deployment. A citation is a claim about where an answer came from, not proof that the answer is correct — and that distinction is the whole difficulty of putting retrieval into real work.

sources.title: This game-playing AI is the new champ at Stratego

items.title: The First AI to Beat Top Stratego Players at a Game of Hidden Pieces
items.body: Stratego is a two-player game of imperfect information: the opponent's piece identities stay hidden, which is why it is used as a benchmark for the strategic thinking of powerful AI models. Researchers from MIT, Carnegie Mellon University, New York University and Stanford developed an AI that defeated top-ranked human Stratego players by a large margin — MIT News describes it as something no AI system had achieved before. The interesting part is what has to be inferred. In a game where you cannot see what you are facing, a strong move depends on reading a hidden board rather than one laid out in front of you.

sources.title: Protests against OpenAI get increasingly creative

discussion.body: The sharpest thing about the piece is its accounting. The wealth and the escape sit on one side of the image; the cost sits on the other. That is a claim about who pays, not a prediction that the technology collapses.
Agreeing that costs are unevenly shared is the easy half. The harder half — who should pay, and through what mechanism — is not something a papier-mâché ship can settle for you.

items.title: The Sinking-Ship Sculpture at the Door of an OpenAI Event
items.body: Two artists from a Bay Area studio unveiled What Iceberg?, a table-sized installation placed at the public entrance to an OpenAI developer event. According to a description of the piece, the 5-foot-tall sculpture shows OpenAI's leaders and investors escaping a sinking ship with unimaginable wealth, while everyone else is left to face the cost of AI. It is a compact piece of political theatre, and the argument it stages is about distribution rather than doom: the escape and the wealth go one way, the bill goes the other.

sources.title: Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems

items.title: Bosnia's Oct. 4 Election: Ethnicity on the Ballot, Emigration on Voters' Minds
items.body: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. Deutsche Welle reports that voters are worried about the economy and emigration, while the campaign has been focused on ethnicity — which the outlet describes as exposing the country's political paralysis. The mismatch is the point: the problems voters name are not the ones the campaign is arguing about.

sources.title: Court halts execution of Christa Gail Pike for a Tennessee murder she committed at age 18

items.title: A Tennessee Execution Was Halted an Hour Before It Was Set to Begin
items.body: Tennessee's execution of a woman for a murder she committed at age 18 was halted Wednesday about an hour before it was scheduled to begin. PBS NewsHour reports that a federal appeals court sought to review whether her allegations of childhood sexual abuse and rape were fully considered at her sentencing. The review turns on the sentencing stage — what that hearing weighed — rather than on the facts of the killing.

sources.title: Build a multi-agent music production pipeline on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime Instances

discussion.body: The load-bearing word here is 'persistent.' Most agent demos are multi-step, not multi-day. The infrastructure question only gets interesting when state has to survive the agents going to sleep and coming back to each other's files.

Persistence may also inherit a new class of failure: whatever a bad run wrote to the shared volume yesterday is what the other two agents open today. Long-lived sessions buy continuity and consequences.

items.title: Why a Multi-Day AI Workflow Needs Different Infrastructure Than a Chatbot
items.body: A lone agent handling customer queries can run in a serverless environment with short-lived sessions. Three agents collaborating on a creative workflow that spans several days — sharing context and building on each other's output — can't: serverless sessions that cap at a few hours don't cut it. That mismatch is the case AWS makes for two compute options on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. MicroVMs are the serverless option, with fast cold starts, session isolation and consumption-based pricing. Runtime Instances are newer: AWS-managed EC2 infrastructure for persistent, long-running agent workflows. Both use the same runtime APIs, but instances add multi-day sessions, GPUs, persistent volumes, and the ability to colocate several agents on one machine. The trade is legible — keep the shared runtime interface, buy duration and hardware. Whether a given pipeline needs it depends on whether the work is genuinely multi-day or merely multi-step.

sources.title: Trump officials changed forms for overseas voters amid a GOP push to restrict voting

items.title: A Last-Minute Pentagon Form Change Cuts a Category of Overseas Voters From Absentee Forms
items.body: NPR reports that the Pentagon made last-minute changes to forms many overseas U.S. citizens use for absentee voting, removing a category of citizens that Republicans have been pushing to block from voting. The reporting characterizes the revision as landing amid that push.

sources.title: MIT Transit Lab to develop an AI platform for public transit agencies

items.title: MIT Transit Lab's Plan for the Fragmented Screens in Transit Control Rooms
items.body: Google.org announced on Sept. 15 that the MIT Transit Lab is a recipient of $2.1 million in funding, one of only 15 projects selected in the worldwide Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation. The funding from Google's philanthropic arm supports NGOs, social enterprises and academic institutions integrating AI-powered solutions across areas such as health, resilience and economy. The lab's winning project, the Public Transit Intelligence Hub, aims to unify transit agencies' real-time monitoring, operations control and passenger communication systems into a single centralized AI-orchestrated platform. The stated goals are better-informed, on-the-spot decisions by control center staff and more immediate, accurate information for riders. The problem being addressed is concrete: transit control centers resemble the movie version of NASA mission control, with staff monitoring radio feeds and screens relaying camera, vehicle, rider and road data — but the information arriving is fragmented rather than integrated into a system with overall awareness of network conditions.

sources.title: NASA has a Dragon dilemma, and there appear to be no good answers

items.title: NASA's Ambition in Orbit: To Be One Customer Among Many
items.body: NASA has spent two decades trying to foster an economy in low-Earth orbit, largely in service to the International Space Station. In recent years that ambition has widened into something bigger: a commercial ecosystem in orbit spanning transportation, space stations, manufacturing and tourism, with NASA itself as one of many customers in the market rather than the anchor owner of everything up there. That distinction is the whole point of the strategy — a market where the government is a buyer among others, not the reason the market exists. Which also means the case for a private station or an orbital factory has to hold up with customers who are not NASA.

sources.title: Police questioning can shape a sexual assault case. Their approach is often wrong

items.title: Most Police Lack Training in Trauma-Informed Interviewing, Experts Say
items.body: A woman's lawsuit alleging a brutal rape is raising questions about how police handle sexual assault cases, NPR reports. Attached to the case is a broader complaint from experts: the majority of police lack adequate training in trauma-informed approaches — the practices meant to keep an investigation from compounding the harm it is supposed to address.

sources.title: 'Crisis of Indigenous child welfare' continues months after Ont. couple's murder trial: advocate

items.title: An Advocate Says a Murder Trial Lit Up Ontario's Indigenous Child-Welfare Crisis
items.body: Jody Harbour, a Halton-based Indigenous advocate, says a months-long murder trial in Milton, Ont., shone a light on what she describes as the continuing crisis of Indigenous child welfare in Ontario. Harbour is named in the report as the person making that argument; the group Grandmother's Voice makes a related one, with its co-founder saying change means ensuring front-line workers know how to support Indigenous people.

sources.title: Lawyer of Junaid Hafeez, a Pakistai scholar imprisoned for 13 years, is hopeful for his release

items.title: A Death Sentence Under Pakistan's Blasphemy Laws, and a Lawyer's Hope
items.body: Junaid Hafeez, a former Fulbright scholar, was sentenced to death in Pakistan under the country's blasphemy laws. DW reports that his family and his lawyer now say there is hope a court will overturn the conviction.

sources.title: Gentle giant Backpack declared winner of Alaska's Fat Bear Week
Meet 'Backpack', the chunky bear who won Fat Bear Week

discussion.body: The category is the charm. Nothing about speed or cleverness — just how much a bear is carrying into winter.
The names are doing more work than the weigh-in. A bear called Backpack plus a fan line about chonk and badonk beats any trophy ceremony.

items.title: Backpack, the Heftiest Bear in Katmai, Is Headed Into Hibernation
items.body: Backpack has won Fat Bear Week after a week of competition, emerging as champion and the heftiest bear in Alaska's Katmai National Park and Preserve, according to PBS NewsHour. One supporter's assessment, reported by the BBC, is that the brown bear has both the chonk and the badonk. The title lands shortly before Backpack enters hibernation, which can last up to six months. There's something appealing about a contest whose criterion is simply mass: most competitions reward what an animal does, and this one rewards what it has managed to put away.

sources.title: Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring

items.title: Ukraine's PM Says Overnight Strikes Hit 11 Regions
items.body: Eleven regions of Ukraine were attacked overnight, with residential buildings and railways also targeted, the country's prime minister said, according to BBC reporting. The account is the Ukrainian government's own summary of the night's strikes.

sources.title: Introducing dots

discussion.body: Proactivity is the whole point. An assistant that waits to be asked is a search box with better manners.
Proactive and in control are two ends of one rope. Every move the assistant makes on its own is a move you didn't make.
Then the feature that matters isn't the initiative, it's the interrupt button.

items.title: OpenAI's Dots Promise Proactivity and Control at the Same Time
items.body: OpenAI has introduced dots, describing them as proactive assistants that can keep working across complex projects and everyday tasks. The company pairs that with a promise about control: that dots help you stay in control while work moves forward. Proactivity and control are the two properties every agent product currently advertises at once, and they are also the two that pull against each other.

sources.title: ‘Sistas’ Producer Courtney Glaudé Set As First Filmmaker Joining Tyler Perry Studios’ Maxscene Division

discussion.body: The phrase doing the work here is 'theatrical opportunities.' A specialty label is a bet that certain films still belong in a room full of strangers rather than a queue, and that bet only pays off if the label keeps signing.
A stated purpose is not a track record. One filmmaker and one film with a teased date tell us the label exists; whether 'theatrical' turns out to mean a real run or a token week is the open question.

items.title: Tyler Perry Studios' New Theatrical Label Signs Its First Filmmaker
items.body: Tyler Perry Studios has a new specialty division, Maxscene, pitched as a home for expanding theatrical opportunities for filmmakers with distinctive voices. Its first signing is Courtney Glaudé, Deadline reports, a producer whose credits include Sistas. Glaudé's first release through the label is Conditioned, a psychological thriller he wrote and directed, with a release date teased for early 2027.

sources.title: Star Trails

items.title: Star Trails, Fishing Boats and City Lights, Seen From 258 Miles Up
items.body: A long-duration image released by NASA shows star trails above Earth, with the blue lights of fishing boats and the yellow lights of Indonesian cities stretched along the scene below. It was taken from the International Space Station as it orbited 258 miles above the Banda Sea on Sept. 20, 2026, and is credited to NASA's Anil Menon. Two kinds of artificial light — working boats and whole cities — sit under the arcs traced by the stars during the exposure.
